filo show PATH... [-r] [--history] [--verify]

  Shows everything the register holds about each file, one after another: what
  filo observed (its path and root, size, modified time, hash, when it was first
  seen, where it was before) and what was decided (its retention, file_date and
  keep_until, and when they were set), then the other files with the same
  content. Nothing is changed.

  A path is looked up in the register, not on the disk, so a missing file is
  shown too, and a file deleted by filo is found by its last path. The modified
  line says whether the file on disk is still as the last scan saw it, from its
  size, modified time and inode, without reading it.

  A directory shows its root, its files by state, the directory rules tried for
  its files in the order they are tried, then its subdirectories (each with how
  many files need a decision) and every file of its own, with its size and
  status.

Flags
  -r, --recursive          directories: list every directory below it too, each
                           with its files
  --history                files: list every path the file has had, newest first
  --verify                 files: read the file and compare its content with the
                           register's hash
